clues: This city stands on a rocky hill in the central part of Anatolia. Old castle ruins still crown the hill in the city's old center.
Far from the sea, this city gets hot dry summers and cold snowy winters. Rain is low and falls mostly in spring and fall, not in summer.
In 1923 a new republic picked this inland city as its capital. It took that role from the old empire's long-time seat of power.
Atatürk founded the new republic and now rests at Anıtkabir, a grand tomb shrine. Each year, crowds mark the day he died at this shrine.
This city is the capital of Turkey, and its top law-making group has its home here. That group is the Grand National Assembly of the land.
